summary: The note describes the Kingdom of Hungary, a monarchy in Central Europe that existed from the Middle Ages into the 20th century, with the stated span 1000–1946 excluding 1918–1920. It traces the origin of the Principality of Hungary to the coronation of Stephen I at Esztergom around the year 1000, and notes that the Árpád dynasty led the monarchy for 300 years. It also states that by the 12th century the kingdom had become a European middle power within the Western world.
one_line: Overview of the Kingdom of Hungary, a Central European monarchy from around 1000 to 1946, founded under Stephen I.
key_facts: The Kingdom of Hungary was a monarchy in Central Europe.
The Kingdom of Hungary existed from the Middle Ages into the 20th century.
The note gives the kingdom's existence as 1000–1946 with the exception of 1918–1920.
The Principality of Hungary emerged as a Christian kingdom upon the coronation of the first king, Stephen I.
Stephen I was crowned at Esztergom around the year 1000.
Stephen I's family, the Árpád dynasty, led the monarchy for 300 years.
By the 12th century, the Kingdom of Hungary had become a European middle power within the Western world.
